def sky_courier(start, missions):
    """Maximize total pay from courier missions flown by an airship.

    The airship begins at integer altitude `start`. Each mission is a tuple
    (req, delta, pay) of ints. You may fly any subset of the missions, in
    any order, one at a time. To fly a mission the current altitude must be
    >= req; completing it changes the altitude by delta (possibly negative)
    and earns pay. The altitude may never become negative: a mission may
    only be flown if the resulting altitude (current + delta) is >= 0.
    Missions not flown have no effect.

    Return the maximum total pay obtainable, as a single int. If no mission
    can be flown (or `missions` is empty), return 0. The answer is a unique
    number, so there is no tie-breaking.

    Input domain (guaranteed):
      0 <= start <= 60
      0 <= len(missions) <= 60
      each (req, delta, pay) satisfies 0 <= req <= 200, -60 <= delta <= 60,
      1 <= pay <= 10**6.

    Note: enumerating subsets and orders is astronomically slow (up to 60!
    orders); a correct solution must exploit structure. Natural greedy
    orderings (by req, by delta, or by pay) are all wrong.

    >>> sky_courier(3, [(0, -4, 100)])
    0
    >>> sky_courier(5, [(5, -3, 10), (2, 4, 7), (8, -8, 100)])
    107
    >>> sky_courier(10, [(10, -6, 5), (4, -4, 5)])
    10
    """
